authoringStatement: A1 expectations were authored before production persistence behavior existed. Mechanical values come from declared formulas and the reviewed plan; checksum goldens were computed by an independent tool, never by the code under test.

classificationPolicy.primary-standard: A current normative Web platform standard.
classificationPolicy.reviewed-contract: A normative repository architecture or package decision.
classificationPolicy.legacy-observation: A reproduced legacy failure the replacement must not preserve.
classificationPolicy.mechanical-derivation: A direct result of a declared formula, integer algorithm, or cap.
classificationPolicy.human-review: A judgment that automation cannot honestly certify.

authorities.source: docs/LEGACY_AUDIT.md — no local recovery, autosave, or dirty indicator; ordinary edits can be lost without recovery
supports: the data-loss regression witness
checksum algorithm sha256-of-sorted-key-json-without-checksum-v1 because it is deterministic, dependency-free, and independently recomputable
envelope byte bounds of 8,000,000 (IndexedDB) and 1,000,000 (localStorage) because the fallback store is shared and synchronous while the primary holds the full candidate comfortably
storage keys changes.recovery.v1:<documentId>:<slot> because keys must embed schema and stable identity and never user text
at most one in-flight write with queued-snapshot replacement because unbounded write queues cannot improve the newest-revision outcome
editing-before-probe downgrades automatic opening to Keep/Discard because silent overwrite of user edits is the worst recoverable failure

authorities.source: Independent sha256 over canonical sorted-key JSON computed at authoring time
